changelog: Core Principles: Removed references to output-format constraints so that all formatting/spacing/punctuation rules live only in [Output Rules]. This prevents accidental restatement of frozen constraints.

When to Segment: Clarified permissive triggers (clause-connectors, commas, parentheticals, fillers) and emphasised conservatism around apparent boundaries (infinitives, possessives, multiword names) without turning common candidates into prohibitions.

Never Segment: Added explicit forbids for splits that are always harmful: separating NP modifiers (including possessive 's, adjective sequences, and essential 'of' complements) from their head nouns, and separating verbs from their essential objects/complements. Each forbid allows an exception when clear punctuation (comma, dash, semicolon, parentheses) marks an explicit break.

Priority Rules: Added scoring guidance for cuts that affect scope/time modifiers (duration, 'only', frequency phrases) and for verb–object adjacency; these receive lowered confidence so they are unlikely to survive tight budgets rather than being removed outright.

Decision Procedure: Removed direct references to [Output Rules] and added a short operational guideline to anticipate the deterministic post-process (density/spacing enforcement) so candidate selection prefers positions that preserve the original tokens and avoid forcing edits; if an exact insertion would require rewriting, choose the nearest legal candidate and mark it with appropriately lower confidence.
